findings.title: Concurrent builds for the same namespace/resource are still unsynchronized
findings.body: Only the final cache assignment is protected. Two concurrent Search requests for an absent index can both observe a cache miss in GetIndex and both execute BuildIndex for the same key. For file-backed indexes, the second bleve.New targets the same directory and can fail; for memory-backed indexes, both builds complete and one fully-built index is silently overwritten in the cache. This also duplicates indexing work and metrics. Synchronize get-or-create/build on a per-key basis (and re-check the cache after acquiring that lock) rather than only locking the map write.

findings.title: Search watch is detached from the ResourceServer shutdown context
findings.body: The startup search watcher is created with context.Background rather than the cancelable context supplied by ResourceServer. Since initialization is now unconditional in NewResourceServer, every configured server starts this watcher during construction, but server.Stop only cancels s.ctx and cannot stop this watch for backends that rely on the passed context. This can leave polling/watch goroutines and backend resources alive after shutdown. Pass the initialization/server context to WatchWriteEvents instead of creating a background context.

findings.title: Closing the search event channel causes a nil-event panic
findings.body: The watcher goroutine receives from events without checking the channel's open status. If a backend closes its event channel during shutdown or on an error, the receive returns nil repeatedly and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type, causing a panic. The goroutine should use `v, ok := <-events` and return when !ok (and ideally also select on its context).

findings.title: The storage-server integration test is now disabled for PostgreSQL in CI
findings.body: PostgreSQL is a supported non-SQLite storage-server backend, but this change skips the only shown integration test for it rather than fixing the failure. As a result, CI will not exercise startup/initialization behavior against PostgreSQL, including the new eager initialization path. The test should be made reliable for PostgreSQL or replaced by an equivalent PostgreSQL-backed test rather than permanently skipped.
